title: Fixed Sum, Biggest Product
statement: Non-negative real numbers $x, y, z$ satisfy $x + y + z = 12$. What is the largest possible value of $xyz$?
insight: AM–GM: the geometric mean is at most the arithmetic mean 4, with equality when all three are equal.
hints: What inequality links a sum and a product?
solution: By AM–GM, $\sqrt[3]{xyz} \le \tfrac{12}{3} = 4$, so $xyz \le 64$, with equality at $x=y=z=4$. (Smoothing view: if two variables differ, replacing both by their average keeps the sum and increases the product.)
